note.en: Vyasa summons Ganesha to write down the Mahabharata as he dictates it.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Section I ("Then Vyasa began to call to mind Ganesa... 'O guide of the Ganas! be thou the writer of the Bharata which I have formed in my imagination'")

verification.notes: Ganguli's Mahabharata Adi Parva Section I records Vyasa calling Ganesa to mind and engaging him as the scribe of the Bharata.

note.en: By this account Ganesha is the scribe who physically wrote the Mahabharata.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Section I ("Then Vyasa began to call to mind Ganesa... 'O guide of the Ganas! be thou the writer of the Bharata which I have formed in my imagination'")

verification.notes: Adi Parva Section I names Ganesa as the writer who set down the Bharata at Vyasa's dictation.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Preface, "The Linga Purana" ("the births of Kartikeya and Ganesa the sons of Siva, and Nandi and Bhringariti his attendants")

verification.notes: Wilson's preface, describing the contents of the Linga Purana, names Kartikeya and Ganesa as the sons of Siva.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Preface, "The Linga Purana" ("the births of Kartikeya and Ganesa the sons of Siva, and Nandi and Bhringariti his attendants")

verification.notes: Wilson's preface names Kartikeya and Ganesa together as the two sons of Siva.

note.en: Andhaka the asura is slain by Shiva; 'slayer of Andhaka' is a standing epithet of Mahadeva in the epic.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section LXXX ("Let salutations be to the slayer of Andhaka, to the father of Kumara, to him who is of blue throat, to him who is the creator")

verification.notes: The Krishna-Arjuna hymn to Mahadeva in Drona Parva Section LXXX salutes Siva as the slayer of Andhaka.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CLV ("even as Mahadeva had slain in days of yore the Asura Andhaka")

verification.notes: Drona Parva Section CLV likens Aswatthaman's kill to the way Mahadeva had slain in days of yore the Asura Andhaka.

note.en: Marichi is one of the nine Brahma-rishis produced from Brahma's mind.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter VII ("Brahma created other mind-born sons, like himself; namely, Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, and Vasishtha: these are the nine Brahmas")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter XV ("they were born the sons of Kasyapa, the son of Marichi, by Aditi, the daughter of Daksha; thence named the twelve Adityas")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter XV calls Kasyapa the son of Marichi when tracing the birth of the twelve Adityas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter VII ("Brahma created other mind-born sons, like himself; namely, Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, and Vasishtha: these are the nine Brahmas")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Daksha together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Atri together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Bhrigu together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Angiras together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Pulastya together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Pulaha together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Kratu together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter VII lists Marichi and Vasishtha together among the nine mind-born sons of Brahma.

note.en: The Gandharvas are among the classes of beings Brahma brings forth in the course of creation.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter V ("The Gandharbas were next born, imbibing melody: drinking of the goddess of speech, they were born, and thence their appellation")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter V places the birth of the Gandharbas among the beings created by Brahma, born imbibing melody.

note.en: The epic's gloss identifies the goddess Gayatri with Savitri, consort of Brahma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCXLI, footnote to Savitri ("Also called Gayatri, the wife of Brahma")

verification.notes: Ganguli's footnote in Vana Parva Section CCXLI glosses Savitri as also called Gayatri, the wife of Brahma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book I, Chapter V ("From his eastern mouth Brahma then created the Gayatri metre, the Rig veda... Gayatri from his skin")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book I, Chapter V pairs the creation of the Gayatri metre with that of the Rig veda from Brahma's eastern mouth.

note.en: Rahu and Ketu are treated as a pair, the two shadowy nodes among the nine planetary bodies.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book II, Chapter XII ("Eight black horses draw the dusky chariot of Rahu... The eight horses of the chariot of Ketu are of the dusky red colour of Lac")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book II, Chapter XII describes the chariots of Rahu and Ketu together in its account of the nine planets.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book II, Chapter XII ("I have thus described to you, Maitreya, the chariots of the nine planets, all which are fastened to Dhruva by aerial cords")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book II, Chapter XII places Ketu's chariot among the nine planets whose orbits it describes alongside the moon's.

note.en: Jagaddhatri is the agent who transfers Devaki's first six conceptions at Vishnu's command.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book V, Chapter II ("The nurse of the universe, Jagaddhatri, thus enjoined by the god of gods, conveyed the six several embryos into the womb of Devaki")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book V, Chapter II records Jagaddhatri, the nurse of the universe, conveying six embryos into the womb of Devaki.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book V, Chapter II ("Jagaddhatri... conveyed the six several embryos into the womb of Devaki, and transferred the seventh after a season to that of Rohini")

verification.notes: Vishnu Purana Book V, Chapter II records Jagaddhatri transferring the seventh embryo to the womb of Rohini.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book V, Chapter II ("The nurse of the universe, Jagaddhatri, thus enjoined by the god of gods, conveyed the six several embryos into the womb of Devaki")

verification.notes: Jagaddhatri is named by that title in Vishnu Purana Book V, Chapter II.

note.en: The Mothers ask Skanda to adopt them, and he accepts them as his mothers.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCXXIX ("Skanda replied, 'O ladies of faultless character, do you accordingly become my mothers. I am your son'")

verification.notes: Vana Parva Section CCXXIX has Skanda accept the goddesses as his mothers.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCXXV ("Let the great Mothers of the Universe repair to-day to Skanda. They can master at will any degree of energy")

verification.notes: Vana Parva Section CCXXV sends the great Mothers of the Universe to Skanda, after which they attend upon him.
